Alright, let’s dive into Chapter 5—Practicing with Intention: The First 20 Hours in Action.
Now that you’ve cleared away the obstacles and built a strong foundation, you’re ready for what really matters: putting in the work, with intention.
The idea is refreshingly simple, but it can be life-changing. Set aside at least 20 hours to truly practice your new skill. Not just going through the motions, but showing up with your full attention, every single time. You want to focus on getting better—on making real progress.
Here’s the thing: it’s not about cramming in as many hours as possible. It’s about the quality of your practice. Think of it like this—would you rather spend hours half-heartedly strumming a guitar, or dedicate a focused, intentional block of time where you really listen, adjust, and improve? That’s where the magic happens.
During each session, you’re not just repeating the same action over and over. You’re watching for mistakes, tweaking your technique, and noticing when something clicks. You’re building confidence, one small win at a time.
Picture this process as a loop. Each time you practice, you try, you learn, you adjust, and then you try again. It’s a cycle that keeps you moving forward, step by step, making sure every minute you invest pays off.
So, as you take on these first 20 hours, remember: intentional practice isn’t just about clocking time. It’s about being present, learning from every attempt, and giving yourself permission to improve. That’s how real progress starts to show up.
